{
  "id": "qatt-figure-row-count",
  "name": "Right To Left Tally",
  "verb": "paint in",
  "idea": "While content loads, each placeholder rises onto the shared baseline and is painted in from its right edge, one child at a time in a right-to-left row at a fixed even step; all stay lit for about a second, then clear quickly and the calm tally starts again.",
  "use": [
    "loading",
    "progress"
  ],
  "trigger": "loop",
  "target": "children",
  "stagger": 90,
  "origin": "50% 100%",
  "keyframes": [
    {
      "offset": 0,
      "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)",
      "transform": "translateY(6px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 100%)",
      "opacity": 0
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.11,
      "easing": "linear",
      "transform": "translateY(0px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)",
      "opacity": 1
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.7,
      "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)",
      "transform": "translateY(0px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)",
      "opacity": 1
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.78,
      "easing": "linear",
      "transform": "translateY(0px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)",
      "opacity": 0
    },
    {
      "offset": 0.79,
      "easing": "linear",
      "transform": "translateY(6px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 100%)",
      "opacity": 0
    },
    {
      "offset": 1,
      "transform": "translateY(6px)",
      "clipPath": "inset(0% 0% 0% 100%)",
      "opacity": 0
    }
  ],
  "timing": {
    "duration": 2400,
    "delay": 0,
    "easing": "linear",
    "iterations": "infinite",
    "direction": "normal",
    "fill": "none"
  },
  "reduced": {
    "kind": "static",
    "note": "The placeholder figures sit still on their baseline, fully painted, while content loads."
  },
  "cardIds": [
    "al-qatt-al-asiri"
  ],
  "lensIds": [
    "qatt-asiri"
  ],
  "culturalNotes": "Follows Al Qatt Al Asiri, the wall painting of Asir in Saudi Arabia, kept and passed down mostly by women who paint on a white gypsum ground in guest rooms. UNESCO lists it as intangible cultural heritage. The motion borrows the rhythm of simple figures repeated at an even step on a shared baseline inside a framed row, so the panel reads as one calm count. It uses only that grammar of repeat and baseline, draws no script, and states no meaning for any figure.",
  "styles": [
    "gulf-arabic-first"
  ]
}

{
 "id": "najdi-door-swing-open",
 "name": "Najdi Panel Step Reveal",
 "verb": "steps open",
 "idea": "Each band of the entry panel opens from right to left behind a triangular leading edge, about 40 ms after the band before it. The edge then flattens and the band settles with a small, heavy drop, so the screen arrives as a row of framed panels rather than as a turning door.",
 "use": [
  "onboarding-slide",
  "hero",
  "card"
 ],
 "trigger": "enter",
 "target": "children",
 "stagger": 40,
 "origin": "100% 50%",
 "keyframes": [
  {
   "offset": 0,
   "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1)",
   "transform": "translateY(3px)",
   "clipPath": "polygon(100% 0%, 100% 0%, 100% 50%, 100% 100%, 100% 100%)",
   "filter": "brightness(1.06)"
  },
  {
   "offset": 0.7,
   "easing": "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1)",
   "transform": "translateY(1px)",
   "clipPath": "polygon(100% 0%, 14% 0%, 0% 50%, 14% 100%, 100% 100%)",
   "filter": "brightness(1.02)"
  },
  {
   "offset": 1,
   "transform": "translateY(0px)",
   "clipPath": "polygon(100% 0%, 0% 0%, 0% 50%, 0% 100%, 100% 100%)",
   "filter": "brightness(1)"
  }
 ],
 "timing": {
  "duration": 240,
  "delay": 0,
  "easing": "linear",
  "iterations": 1,
  "direction": "normal",
  "fill": "both"
 },
 "reduced": {
  "kind": "fade",
  "ms": 200,
  "note": "The panel bands fade in together over 200 ms, with no wipe or drop."
 },
 "cardIds": [
  "najdi-painted-doors"
 ],
 "lensIds": [],
 "culturalNotes": "Follows the painted wooden doors of the mud-brick building tradition of Najd in central Arabia, made and painted by Najdi builders and craftsmen. The motion borrows only the construction: triangles set in rows inside framed panels become the stepped leading edge of each band, and the weight of the earth wall becomes the flat, matte settle. The reveal runs right to left to suit an Arabic-first layout. It does not copy any specific heritage door or site, and it uses no flag or emblem.",
 "styles": [
  "gulf-arabic-first"
 ]
}
